original_value: This paper proposes a robust and real-time capable algorithm for classification of the first and second heart sounds. The classification algorithm is based on the evaluation of the envelope curve of the phonocardiogram. For the evaluation, in contrast to other studies, measurements on 12 probands were conducted in different physiological conditions. Moreover, for each measurement the auscultation point, posture and physical stress were varied. The proposed envelope-based algorithm is tested with two different methods for envelope curve extraction: the Hilbert transform and the short-time Fourier transform. The performance of the classification of the first heart sounds is evaluated by using a reference electrocardiogram. Overall, by using the Hilbert transform, the algorithm has a better performance regarding the F1-score and computational effort. The proposed algorithm achieves for the S1 classification an F1-score up to 95.7% and in average 90.5%. The algorithm is robust against the age, BMI, posture, heart rate and auscultation point (except measurements on the back) of the subjects.

result.paraphrase: This paper presents a robust, real-time-capable algorithm for classifying the first and second heart sounds. The method relies on analyzing the phonocardiogram envelope curve. Unlike other studies, evaluation was performed using measurements from 12 subjects under varying physiological conditions; for each recording, the auscultation point, posture, and physical stress were also varied. The proposed envelope-based algorithm was assessed with two envelope-extraction methods: the Hilbert transform and the short-time Fourier transform. Performance for first-heart-sound classification was measured using a reference electrocardiogram. Overall, the Hilbert transform yielded better F1-score performance and lower computational effort. For S1 classification, the algorithm achieved an F1-score of up to 95.7% and an average of 90.5%. It is robust to subjects’ age, BMI, posture, heart rate, and auscultation point, except for measurements taken on the back.
